extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies and other state plan developers (and affected EGUs, utilities, reliability authorities, and stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for states to develop and submit state plans implementing EPA emission guidelines for existing electric generating units (EGUs), including requirements for meaningful engagement, transparency, reporting, and compliance assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful engagement (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: “timely engagement with pertinent stakeholders and/or their representatives in the plan development or plan revision process.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final subpart Ba revisions define meaningful engagement with this phrase; such engagement should be timely and occur during plan development or revision. The definition also provides that engagement “should not be disproportionate in favor of certain stakeholders and should be informed by available best practices.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Pertinent stakeholders (definition and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pertinent stakeholders “include, but are not limited to, industry, small businesses, and communities most affected by and/or vulnerable to the impacts of the plan or plan revision.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should identify and engage pertinent stakeholders using targeted knowledge of state- and source-specific circumstances. The preamble notes states' diversity and thus does not impose additional identification requirements; states should tailor stakeholder lists accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include communities affected by climate change
rubrics_metrics.description: States' pertinent stakeholders are expected to include communities within the state that are most affected by and/or vulnerable to the impacts of climate change (e.g., those exposed to more extreme drought, flooding, extreme heat and cold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects states to refer to section III of the preamble on climate impacts to assist in identifying these stakeholders. Commenters supported including those impacted by climate change as pertinent stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include communities near EGUs and pipelines
rubrics_metrics.description: States should include communities located near affected EGUs and those near pipelines, who may experience impacts associated with construction and operation of infrastructure required under a state plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities related to construction/operation of new natural gas and CO2 pipelines may impact individuals locally and at larger distances; states should consider both local proximity and broader impacts from infrastructure when identifying stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include energy communities and energy workers
rubrics_metrics.description: States are expected to include energy communities impacted by each affected EGU, including energy workers employed at affected EGUs (operation and maintenance), workers who may construct/install pollution controls, and workers in associated industries (fuel extraction/delivery, CO2 transport/storage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA encourages states to consider Federal programs that support these communities, to take advantage of workforce assistance resources, and to consider workforce data transparency and workforce transition planning (e.g., Colorado law example). States are encouraged to provide such data during meaningful engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include balancing authorities and reliability coordinators
rubrics_metrics.description: States should include relevant balancing authorities, systems operators, and reliability coordinators that maintain electric reliability as pertinent stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These entities need visibility into unit-specific compliance plans. Early notification and periodic follow up on unit-specific decisions (e.g., control installation, voluntary cease operation choices and timeframes) will assist reliability planning authorities and help prevent reliability issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider overburdened communities and cumulative impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: States should consider communities overburdened by existing air pollution (greenhouse gases and co-pollutants) and the cumulative burden of pollution when identifying pertinent stakeholders, since these populations may be especially vulnerable to plan impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA urges states to consider cumulative impacts (citing California, New Jersey examples) and notes the Agency's work to prioritize cumulative impacts research and integrate cumulative impacts into EPA work. Meaningful engagement should allow identification of facility- and community-specific cumulative stressors and vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of meaningful engagement in plan submittal (four required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must describe: (1) a list of the pertinent stakeholders identified by the state; (2) a summary of engagement conducted; (3) a summary of the stakeholder input received; and (4) a description of how stakeholder input was considered in plan development or plan revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will review state plans for inclusion of these required descriptions as part of completeness evaluation. Failure to include required elements for notice and opportunity for public participation (including procedural requirements at 40 CFR 60.23a(i) and 60.27a(g)(2)(ix)) may be grounds for finding a submission incomplete or for disapproval where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced participation, transparency, and accessible notice
rubrics_metrics.description: In conducting meaningful engagement, states should allow for balanced participation (including communities most vulnerable), ensure information is timely and transparent, and provide adequate and accessible notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internet notice alone may be insufficient; states should consider prominent advertisement (newspapers, libraries, schools, hospitals, travel centers, community centers, places of worship, gas stations, convenience stores, casinos, smoke shops, Tribal Assistance for Needy Families offices, Indian Health Services, clinics, and other community health/social services). States should consider geographic, linguistic, and other barriers to participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor engagement strategy to identified stakeholders and state circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: States should develop a strategy for engagement with identified pertinent stakeholders that is tailored to state- and source-specific circumstances, recognizing state diversity in local conditions, resources, and established practices of engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA provides discussion of potential impacts and best practices but is not finalizing additional identification requirements; states are expected to use targeted local knowledge to hone stakeholder identification and the engagement strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specific data types in meaningful engagement documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: States' demonstration may include data received from stakeholders such as population/demographics of communities near EGUs/pipelines, identification/data on overburdened communities vulnerable to plan impacts, data on energy workers affected by compliance strategies, workforce needs (expected jobs, skills required), and data on communities near state/Tribal borders if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA encourages inclusion of such data in the plan submittal's demonstration of meaningful engagement to help analyze impacts and tailor responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EPA and federal tools/resources to identify impacted communities
rubrics_metrics.description: States and stakeholders are encouraged to use EPA resources such as unit-level proximity analysis, the Power Plant Environmental Justice Screening Methodology (PPSM), EJScreen, and federal resources like the Energy Communities Interagency Working Group Clearinghouse to identify populations and areas potentially exposed or overburdened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools provide census block group level info on exposure and socioeconomic characteristics, emission implications of controls (e.g., CCS), and federal funding opportunities relevant to energy communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion on form of enforceable commitment for permanent cessation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not finalizing a requirement that commitments to permanently cease operation must take the form of an emission limit of 0 lb CO2/MWh; it is within the state's discretion to create enforceable commitments in the form it deems appropriate (state regulation, permit, order, or other legal instrument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an emission limit or other requirement that creates an enforceable commitment is included in a title V permit before EPA approves the state plan, that condition must be labeled “state-only” or “state-only enforceable” until EPA approval, after which the permit should be revised to make it federally enforceable. States should be cautious because state instruments can be revised without revising the state plan, potentially undermining integrity if not properly codified in the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require compliance with permanent cessation legal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans that include EGUs planning to permanently cease operation must require those EGUs to comply with applicable state and Federal requirements for permanently ceasing operation, including removal from the state's air emissions inventory and amending or revoking permits to reflect permanent shutdown status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinforces application of existing state and Federal laws and ensures orderly administration and transparency of the emission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require publicly accessible unit-level reporting websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Each state plan must require owners/operators of affected EGUs to establish publicly accessible “Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs” websites to post all reporting and recordkeeping information for each affected EGU subject to the state plan (emissions data, information relevant to compliance, increments of progress, milestones, extension requests, and any information required to be submitted as part of the state plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although data are also submitted to EPA and state agencies, EPA requires broad and timely public access; data should be available in a readily downloadable format. EPA disagrees that this is duplicative, citing unique reporting requirements under the emission guidelines (e.g., increments of progress). Some commenters expressed burden concerns and asked for format/notification specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report deviations from increments/milestones within 30 business days
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must report any deviation from any federally enforceable state plan increment of progress or reporting milestone within 30 business days after the owner/operator knew or should have known of the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report must explain causes of the deviation, describe measures taken or to be taken to cure the deviation and prevent recurrence (including timeframes), be submitted to the state regulatory agency, and concurrently be posted to the affected EGU's public website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting (CAA §114) for EGUs planning permanent cessation before 1/1/2032
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing coal-fired steam generating EGUs in existence as of a state plan submission that plan to cease operating before Jan 1, 2032 must comply with reporting requirements under CAA section 114(a). Five years before any planned cessation date (or by state plan submission date, whichever is later) the owner/operator must submit an initial report with: (1) a summary of process steps and timing to cease operation and any notification requirements, and (2) supporting regulatory documents and filings (RTO/ISO correspondence, SEC filings, integrated resource plans, PUC orders, reliability analyses, notices altering timing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each remaining year prior to the committed date, the operator must submit annual status reports documenting progress on steps and new supporting documents. A final report is required within 6 months after the committed closure date documenting actions taken to ensure cessation is permanent. Under CAA §114 these requirements are limited to reporting (no milestones). EPA requires these reports to preserve rule integrity and detect changes if a unit's plan to cease changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term reliability mechanism as alternative to ACO reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is providing that states may include in their state plans a short-term reliability mechanism allowing affected EGUs to comply with an emission limitation corresponding to their baseline emission rate during periods of grid emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism is intended to allow states to respond quickly to emergency situations and avoid affected EGUs being out of compliance or needing administrative compliance orders (ACOs). EPA is not finalizing a general ACO-application approach for reliability and believes structural changes and mechanisms provided in the final rule reduce need for ACOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan submission deadline (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must be submitted 24 months after publication of the final emission guidelines in the Federal Register (superseding subpart Ba's default timeline of 18 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA determined 24 months is necessary given the complexity of the source category and the need for analysis, consultation, and coordination among states, utilities, reliability authorities, and owners/operators. The final rule also reduces the number of affected EGUs relative to proposal, but EPA retained the 24‑month timeline.
